I mean, most of the time, I don't check my phone every five minutes, and I usually have the sound turned off. Sometimes I just don't notice the messages, and other times I don't feel like responding immediately. I guess I don't want to feel obligated to pick up my phone every time it buzzes. If something is really important, people can call me, right? Otherwise, I'll respond when I feel like it. But then, my friend who was slightly drunk told me that I'm being a dick for not responding right away. He said that it barely takes any time to respond and that it implies I don't care about others. I can see his point, but for me, it's more about the principle of the matter. I don't want to feel like I'm forced to give attention whenever someone sends me a message. I want to have control over when I engage in conversations. So, is it wrong to not always respond immediately? Or is it okay to set boundaries like this? I'm not sure. Maybe I should think about how this affects my relationships with others. If most people are fine with it, as I've noticed, then maybe it's not a big deal. But if it upsets some people, like my friend, then maybe I need to reconsider. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can respond within a few hours instead of waiting too long, or set specific times to check my messages. That way, I'm not ignoring people completely, but I'm also not tied to my phone all the time. It might help balance my need for autonomy with others' expectations of prompt responses. Another thing to consider is the context of the messages. If someone sends a message that seems urgent, I should probably respond as soon as I can. But if it's something casual, like a "Hey, how are you?" or a joke, then taking a little time to respond shouldn't be a problem. It's important to communicate my boundaries clearly so that people understand my approach to messaging. I also think about how technology has changed communication. We're so used to instant replies, but that doesn't mean we have to respond immediately. It's okay to take a moment to process and respond thoughtfully rather than just reacting right away. This could actually improve the quality of our conversations. In the end, I believe it's about finding a balance that works for me while respecting the feelings and expectations of others. Setting clear boundaries and communicating them can help prevent misunderstandings and maintain healthy relationships. It's not about being right or wrong, but about finding a way to interact that feels authentic and respectful to everyone involved.
